docs.title: MSF Laravel GraphQL
docs.text: msflib/graphql is the shared GraphQL integration layer for the MSF Laravel ecosystem. It packages the Laravel and Lighthouse conventions needed to expose GraphQL in a consistent, reusable way across downstream packages and apps.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package provides:

  • Lighthouse integration and configuration
  • reusable GraphQL base utilities and service registration
  • a consistent schema bootstrap path for the rest of the MSF stack
  • a shared GraphQL dependency layer that other packages can build on top of

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• keep schema conventions consistent and reusable
  • prefer centralized GraphQL wiring over app-specific registration
  • keep the package focused on the GraphQL foundation rather than business logic

docs.title: Package overview
docs.text: The msflib/graphql package is the reusable GraphQL foundation for the MSF Laravel ecosystem. It centralizes the Lighthouse-based integration pattern so downstream packages can rely on a consistent GraphQL setup.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is intended to cover:

  • Laravel provider registration
  • Lighthouse integration and schema discovery
  • shared GraphQL conventions for downstream packages
  • reusable schema and support patterns used by the wider stack

docs.title: Expected integration pattern
docs.text:
The package participates in Laravel via Composer and a service provider registration in composer.json:

"extra": {
  "laravel": {
    "providers": [
      "Msflib\\GraphQl\\MsfGraphQlServiceProvider"
    ]
  }
}

This keeps the package discoverable in the host Laravel app without custom bootstrapping in each project.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use Msflib\GraphQl\MsfGraphQlServiceProvider;

The package is typically consumed as a dependency by other MSF libraries and apps, rather than as a business application in its own right.

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• prefer reusable schema conventions over application-specific behavior
  • keep GraphQL concerns centralized in this package
  • document integration points clearly for downstream packages
  • validate changes with the package's local test workflow
